**1) LAYOUT**
*   **Window:** 1024x768 (Maximized). Standard Windows 11 chrome (Title bar + Taskbar).
*   **Sidebar (Left):** [0, 68] to [275, 946]. Width ~275px. Contains navigation sections.
    *   **Section "Data Recovery":** [0, 95] to [275, 325]. Contains 3 list items.
    *   **Section "Advanced Features":** [0, 365] to [275, 525]. Contains 2 list items.
    *   **Section "File Backup":** [0, 565] to [275, 650]. Contains 1 list item.
*   **Main Content Area (Right):** [280, 68] to [1024, 946].
    *   **Header Panel:** [282, 58] to [998, 248]. Dark grey background. Contains primary instruction text and a sub-header ("Internal drives").
    *   **Modal/Overlay Dialog ("Unable to find your hard drive?"):** [282, 238] to [998, 946]. White background, rounded corners, drop shadow. Overlays the main content.
        *   **Dialog Header:** [290, 260] to [990, 310]. Title + Close icon.
        *   **Tab Bar:** [320, 395] to [720, 445]. Centered. Two tabs: "Select Location" (Active), "Device Detection" (Inactive).
        *   **Instructional Text Block:** [325, 495] to [900, 600].
        *   **Device Grid:** [325, 620] to [960, 920]. 2-column layout (Left col: Physical Disks, Right col: Partitions).
            *   **Left Column (Disks):** Width ~300px. Items: "Virtual_Disk NVME Pre...", "Microsoft NVMe Direct ...".
            *   **Right Column (Partitions):** Width ~400px. Items: "Recovery", "Windows(C:)", "Temp(D:)".
        *   **Footer Action:** [855, 865] to [970, 910]. "Got it" button aligned right.

*   **Button Height:** ~40px - 44px.

*   **Progress Bar Height:** ~4px - 6px.

*   **Border Radius (Dialog):** ~8px - 12px.
*   **Icon in Partition Cards:** 32x32px or 40x40px (HDD icon).

**6) CONTROLS & STATES**
*   **Window Controls:** Minimize, Maximize/Restore, Close (Top Right). State: Normal.
*   **Sidebar List Items:**
    *   "Hardware Disk": **Selected** (Blue left border indicator, light blue background, green checkmark badge on right).
    *   "SD Card": Normal.
    *   "More Recovery Tools": Normal.
*   **Dialog Close Button ('X'):** Top right of dialog. State: Normal/Hoverable.
*   **Tabs:**
    *   "Select Location": **Selected/Active** (White background, blue bottom border or shadow, bold text).
    *   "Device Detection": **Inactive** (Transparent background, grey text).
*   **Primary Buttons ("Search Entire Disk", "Got it"):** State: Normal (Solid Blue fill, white text). Hover likely darkens blue.
*   **Info Icon:** Circle-'i' next to dialog title. State: Normal.
*   **Scroll Bar:** Visible on the right edge of the dialog content area. Thumb visible indicating scrollable content.

**7) ICONOGRAPHY**
*   **Style:** Flat, Outline/Filled hybrid (mostly filled shapes with simple geometry), consistent stroke width (likely 1.5px or 2px).
*   **Title Bar Icons:** Cloud (filled blue), Cart (outline), Target/Bullseye (outline), Info (outline), Menu (hamburger).
*   **Sidebar Icons:**
    *   Hardware Disk: Grid of squares (blue filled).
    *   SD Card: SD card shape (grey outline).
    *   More Tools: Wrench/Screwdriver cross (grey outline).
    *   File Repair: Document with wrench (grey outline).
    *   Partition Rescue: Life preserver (grey outline).
    *   Backup: Clock/History icon (grey outline).
*   **Device Icons (in cards):**
    *   Physical Drives: No icon shown (text only) OR implicit.
    *   Partitions: Generic Hard Drive icon (Grey cylinder shape).
*   **Badges:**
    *   Checkmark (Green circle).
    *   Question Mark (White circle with '?' for Recovery partition).

**8) STATE**
*   **Page State:** **Partial / Overlay / Assisted Flow**.
    *   The underlying state is "Select Location" (initial step of recovery).
    *   The capture shows an **Interruption/Assistant Overlay** triggered by the condition "Unable to find your hard drive?" (or user clicked help). This is an educational modal guiding the user to scan the entire disk instead of a partition.
*   **Motion Cues:** None explicitly captured, but the modal implies a "pop-up" entrance. The scrollbar suggests the list of devices might be longer than the visible area.
